executionHistory.summary: Stabilize phase over the operational behaviour of what this packet actually changed: tests/e2e/assistant/required_no_skip_guard_test.go, plus the test lane carrying it. The question was narrow - the fix is a guard that runs go/parser over source at test time, so does the guard itself introduce flake, cost, or a hidden environmental coupling. SIX findings, all evidence-backed. (1) COST: executed the two guard tests through ./smackerel.sh test unit --go --go-run, exit 0; the tests/e2e/assistant package reported 0.009s for 2 tests plus 7 subtests. Work is fixed at five os.ReadFile plus five parser.ParseFile with SkipObjectResolution, plus seven in-memory fixture parses; the denylist is a five-entry compile-time literal so cost cannot grow as the directory grows. The 28.4s wall figure is the whole focused lane including container start and compile, not the guard. (2) DETERMINISM: a read-only search for os.Getwd, relative-path literals, Getenv, time.Now, rand and net/http in the guard returned NO match (exit 1). It has exactly two inputs - runtime.Caller(0), a compile-time constant, and five file reads. No clock, RNG, env, goroutine, socket, container or live stack, so there is no varying input for flake to come from. Adversarial fixtures are in-memory strings and cannot be picked up by the production directory scan. (3) WORKING DIRECTORY: independence holds. The scan dir is anchored on runtime.Caller(0), never on CWD, so the process working directory cannot change the verdict. The real coupling is to the source tree existing at the compile-time path, which holds by construction here because the Go lane compiles and runs in ONE container invocation against ONE mount - verified -v SCRIPT_DIR:/workspace with -w /workspace at smackerel.sh lines 129/133 and 1201/1204. The single input that would break it is -trimpath, verified ABSENT from every shell, Dockerfile, compose, workflow and Makefile surface in the repo; and were it introduced the guard fails LOUD, because each unreadable required file appends a violation ending in t.Fatalf. Fail-closed is the correct direction of error for this guard, so the silent-green class cannot recur through that path. Recorded as a Discovered Issues row with disposition accepted-as-designed. (4) BUILD-TAG ISOLATION is the property that makes the fix durable, and it is verified: exactly 1 of 48 .go files in tests/e2e/assistant omits //go:build e2e, and it is the guard, so under a plain go test ./... the assistant_e2e package compiles from the guard alone. Finding 1 proves this happens in practice - that run carried no e2e tag and the package still executed. A guard that only runs when the gated suite runs could not detect the gated suite silently not running, which is exactly BUG-069-005. (5) FLOCK SUITE LOCK / EXIT 73: assessed and judged NOT a defect and NOT this packet's work. smackerel.sh lines 569 and 578 use the non-blocking flock -n and print a named remediation before exit 73, so the refusal is designed rather than accidental. The descriptor is opened with exec FD-redirect, so the advisory lock is kernel-released on process death and no stale-lock class exists - which is why the earlier exit 73 in this session cleared with no intervention. Verified NOW: three zero-byte lock files persist from 07:08 and 07:11 with ZERO holders under fuser and no live smackerel.sh test runner, so the locks are free and the files are inert. The mechanism by which an orphan can hold one is descriptor inheritance, since children inherit the FD and a detached descendant outliving its parent keeps the lock alive. On ownership, smackerel.sh does not appear in this packet's Change Boundary allowed implementation path set in scopes.md, so it is recorded as an observation against smackerel.sh lines 552-583 in Discovered Issues rather than claimed as packet work. (6) REQUIRED-TEST DETERMINISM: independent confirmation taken fresh at the current revision - TestRequiredAssistantE2ETestsNeverSkip passing means it re-read all five files, located all five declarations and found zero t.Skip-family calls in their bodies, and a missing declaration is fatal there so the pass also proves none was renamed or deleted. VERDICT: STABLE. No remediation was required inside the Change Boundary, so no fix was applied and no route was raised. executionHistory.summary: Security phase bounded to what BUG-069-005 changed: the required-test no-skip guard, the F069-INTENT-COMPILER-DISABLED coherence check, the compiled-intent execution path, and the five manifest-required tests. The confirm machine, conversation store, and HTTP adapter were read because the changed surface calls into them. VERDICT: FINDINGS - one MEDIUM, three LOW; no critical/high, no authorization break, no credential exposure. (1) CONFIRM REPLAY, the question that mattered most: sequential replay protection is REAL IN THE CODE and not merely test-asserted - Machine.Confirm clears PendingConfirm and persists that clear before the facade reaches actionExecutor.Execute, so a second sequential confirm returns ErrPendingNotFound and renders StatusUnavailable/ErrNoMatch; the path also re-verifies user/transport/ref/schema against the server-owned persisted payload, which the test does not depend on. BUT SEC-069-005-1 (MEDIUM, OWASP A04 TOCTOU): that single-flight property does not hold under concurrency. Machine.Confirm is load-check-persist across three separate store calls; grep for 'FOR UPDATE|pg_advisory|BeginTx|.Begin(|sync.Mutex|sync.RWMutex' over machine.go and pg_store.go returned exit 1 (no match), grep for mutex/singleflight over facade.go returned exit 1, and PGStore.Persist is an unconditional INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE with no version or confirm_ref predicate. The transport does not close it either: turnDedupKey is {userDigest, transport, messageID}, keyed on transport_message_id and NOT on confirm_ref, so two POSTs sharing one confirm_ref with different message ids both take an owner lease and both reach the executor. The code comment claiming single-flight defeats a race against the AUDIT write, not against the PENDING check that gates execution. The required test covers the sequential case only (a third sequential turn; no go func, no WaitGroup), so this is a coverage boundary and a different defect class, not a new false green. Rated MEDIUM not HIGH because it needs an authenticated actor racing their own confirm with no cross-user reach on a single-operator local-first product; not LOW because it falsifies an invariant the code states and the remedy is small. ROUTED to bubbles.implement, deliberately not fixed here: the change lands in confirm/machine.go and context/pg_store.go, product runtime files outside this packet's Change Boundary, and would bypass the test phase such a change requires. (2) CROSS-USER REDEMPTION: NO, and structurally so. Both redemption paths resolve pending state from the caller's own conversation loaded by (UserID, Transport) and only then compare the reference; no lookup is keyed on the reference alone, so another user's reference is unreachable rather than merely hard to guess. The precondition holds: httpadapter sets userID from auth.UserIDFromContext and returns 401 auth_required otherwise, and TurnRequest carries no identity field at all, which is exactly what Gate G047 requires. SEC-069-005-2 (LOW): the disambiguation ref is fmt.Sprintf("disambig-location-%d", emittedAt.UnixNano()) - predictable, not exploitable today, recorded because that safety depends on the lookup shape staying as it is. Shared-token deployments collapsing onto SharedUserID is declared behaviour (F-069-USERID-BINDING), stated plainly and not counted as a finding. (3) GUARD INTEGRITY: the FATAL-on-missing claim is TRUE and verified against source - scanRequiredTestBodyForSkips returns errRequiredNoSkipTestMissing, the caller appends a violation, and t.Fatalf fires, so renaming or deleting a required test fails the guard; an unreadable file is a violation and an empty denylist is its own t.Fatal, and the adversarial subtest proves it by execution. SEC-069-005-3 (LOW): two residual evasions remain - an indirect skip via a helper is invisible because detection is body-scoped, and a receiver not named t does not match the regex; the direct t.Skipf form that caused THIS bug is caught. SEC-069-005-4 (LOW): the five-entry denylist has no runtime cross-check against scenario-manifest.json, so removing one entry narrows coverage silently. (4) CONFIG COHERENCE: F069-INTENT-COMPILER-DISABLED genuinely REFUSES - it is a return fmt.Errorf at assistant.go:557, contrasted with rule #4 twenty lines later which uses slog.Warn and continues. The apparent bypass via blanking the compilerConfigLoaded antecedent was checked rather than assumed and does not work: mustString("ASSISTANT_INTENT_COMPILER_MODEL_ROLE") makes an empty value a fatal F068-SST-MISSING one layer up, and the SST pins model_role as a REQUIRED non-empty literal, so the check is effectively unconditional in any bootable config.
